f4b4bb981e:5cfad72d0581f201.title: ZILART Museum
f4b4bb981e:5cfad72d0581f201.summary: ZILART is a new museum of contemporary art in Moscow. Its building is a copper-clad cube with carefully balanced proportions, measuring 60 × 60 meters at its base and rising 36 meters high. The museum's visual voice is a custom typeface, ZILART, defined by asymmetric proportions and an expressive rhythm. Designed with the museum's architectural scale in mind, it works across Cyrillic and Latin scripts, from the logo to typography on copper and concrete surfaces, posters, and digital screens. The identity becomes part of the museum's architecture through large-scale typography, gallery numbers conceived as sculptural objects, wayfinding, entrance design, and digital displays. Mint and deep green create a counterpoint to the warm copper facade, while graphite and natural tones complement the building's materiality. For the museum shop, Collection, we developed a range of publications and objects, including collaborations with contemporary artists.

f4b4bb981e:36e78103bbe0d863.title: OASE : A new skincare system for Mars
f4b4bb981e:36e78103bbe0d863.summary: On Mars, skin spends most of the day sealed inside a suit. Weeks of friction and repeated irritation leave a barrier that has no time to recover. OASE is a speculative skincare brand for the first settlers on Mars. Instead of prescribing products for a fixed skin type, it tracks how skin responds as people move between the airlock, living quarters and sleep pods, and adjusts care as those responses change. The name comes from oasis. Mars once held water, and traces of it still remain in its rock. OASE takes that idea as its premise: a small source of care in an environment that offers none. Care runs on the O.A.S.I.S. protocol, a five-step cycle (Observe, Assess, Separate, Invigorate, Sync) that begins again once it ends. It is delivered through a single kit that combines a smart mirror, a skincare device and four cosmetic products. f4b4bb981e:f4219e26c2845ba2.title: El Capricho de Gaudí
f4b4bb981e:f4219e26c2845ba2.summary: El Capricho, also known as Villa Quijano, is one of the few buildings Antoni Gaudí completed outside Catalonia. Built in Comillas between 1883 and 1885 for Máximo Díaz de Quijano, it is laid out to follow the sun from room to room, which earned it the nickname of the architectural sunflower. Today it is run as a cultural space that welcomes thousands of visitors a month, from families and school groups to international tourists. Its image had not kept pace with that role. The brand needed to work across tickets, signage, workshops, merchandise, digital channels and the building's 140th anniversary, and it had to do so without ever competing with the building it represents. The question was how to change the image of a Gaudí building, and who should be part of that decision.

f4b4bb981e:bac771e2414d976e.summary: Local Local is an urban inspiration hub with cultural consciousness. A remotely controllable space rooted in the local area. It's a café, an art gallery, a blank canvas, a portal to the depths of one's thouts, a transit point to everything. We seek breakthroughs within reality, and opportunities within those breakthroughs. Local Local cherishes every moment of pause, capturing instances that transcend daily routines, and preparing for future moments of sudden inspiration. The only limit here is the prohibition against stopping your imagination. It's a space for every free spirit to enjoy a relaxed lifestyle that is true to the present, inspiring the now, and can be enjoyed anytime, anywhere. We aim to create an urban inspiration capsule with a sense of city environment awareness and cultural consciousness.

f4b4bb981e:c51e5baede298a64.title: Città di Ancona
f4b4bb981e:c51e5baede298a64.summary: Ancona was born from geography: a promontory that bends into the sea, a natural feature that the ancients recognized and called "Ankón," the "elbow" of Italy. This singular curve, where the land embraces the sea, defines not only the morphology of the city, but also its cultural, economic, and symbolic identity. It is a shape that embodies both function and metaphor: shelter and openness, protection and horizon.

f4b4bb981e:d8d905b1028d6393.summary: Minimal Improvements is a production masterclass community founded by seasoned producer Francesco, aka Distilled Noise, championing process over shortcuts and originality over formula. Inspired by the interfaces and workflows of DAWs, we created a motion-first, modular identity that evolves through layering, arranging and refining. Balancing flexibility with typographic clarity, the system mirrors the creative process itself, giving the brand consistency without constraining its expression.

f4b4bb981e:288268e8295f7cee.title: Solune ? Brand Identity Design
f4b4bb981e:288268e8295f7cee.summary: Solune | Strategy & Visual Identity Brand strategy, visual identity, and motion design for Solune, a forward thinking solar energy brand redefining how renewable energy is captured, stored, and distributed. Built around the idea of Energy Beyond Daylight, the identity combines geometric precision, bold typography, and a distinctive color palette to create a modern and recognizable brand system. The identity comes to life through motion design by Jon Nuredini, bringing an additional layer of energy and movement to the visual experience.

f4b4bb981e:4d5de39b5b3668fb.title: Away
f4b4bb981e:4d5de39b5b3668fb.summary: "Away". Through a quiet white opening, distant worlds begin to appear. A city glowing at the sunset, a landscape untouched, a place that feels both familiar and impossibly far away. Each frame becomes a little window onto somewhere else. An invitation to wander, to dream, and to travel.

f4b4bb981e:acd8f47bb40f24a7.title: a to A
f4b4bb981e:acd8f47bb40f24a7.summary: ?a to A? is a future exhibition set in 2051, exploring 127, a countercultural movement that emerged twenty years earlier.?In 2031, as AI began to predict and evaluate human behavior, some people disconnected from centralized AI and turned to personal servers and local AI. ?a to A? archives how the equipment that began as a means of independence gradually became a symbol of identity and evolved into a form of countercultural fashion.

f4b4bb981e:d76ae412082ab5dc.title: The Red Car - Traveling and scouting Iceland
f4b4bb981e:d76ae412082ab5dc.summary: A 1985 Mercedes-Benz camper, known simply as the red car. I've driven it across Iceland and into the Highlands, through every kind of weather, using it as a base for traveling, photographing and scouting locations. These photographs turn the camera back on the vehicle itself, placing its familiar red shape in the landscapes I've been exploring. They document the journeys and stops along the way, from rough Highland tracks to quiet campsites.

f4b4bb981e:d0e1f30ecc70a48f.summary: The project, developed in collaboration with the Adam Mickiewicz Institute (IAM) team and the Culture.pl editorial team, aimed to build relationships with artists and creative communities (IAM visual identity) and present Polish culture and its creators to an international audience (Culture.pl). IAM works with artists and people in the cultural sector who think outside the box, experiment, challenge existing ideas and take risks. We wanted the Institute's visual identity to reflect this open and bold approach, while giving space to the work itself. Rather than compete with the artists' work for attention, the visual identity provides a clear, distinctive and flexible frame for presenting it.

f4b4bb981e:c460ad19d835a4f4.title: Noche en Blanco Málaga 2026
f4b4bb981e:c460ad19d835a4f4.summary: LNEB es un evento dedicado a la creación cultural en Málaga, que acoge actividades, exposiciones y propuestas artísticas abiertas al público. Esta edición se desarrolla bajo el lema "El futuro se escribe con música", una temática que toma la música como punto de partida para conectar cultura, innovación y participación ciudadana. Para su identidad visual nos hemos inspirado en el movimiento y la vibración del sonido. La propuesta se construye a partir de una tipografía variable y un sistema gráfico vivo, capaz de transformarse y reaccionar a la música. Las formas circulares que componen las letras hacen referencia a los ciclos lunares, conectando visualmente con el imaginario del evento. El sistema visual se expande mediante texturas, deformaciones y animaciones influenciadas por el Op Art, utilizando colores vibrantes y contrastados que refuerzan el carácter del evento. La identidad busca convertirse en una experiencia dinámica e interactiva.

a4977d3fa4:215021acea1cd244.title: The NEEDLES x Pendleton Collection Puts Six Pieces of Archival Wool to Work
a4977d3fa4:215021acea1cd244.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:215021acea1cd244.summary: Summary NEEDLES and Pendleton link up for the first time on a six-piece capsule cut from Pendleton’s traditional plaids and wool fabricsA boxy shirt, a jacket with leather elbow patches and a coat in an archival Pendleton pattern lead the outerwear and shirtingPlaid trousers, a mohair sweater in Pendleton’s signature Native-inspired motif and a fully lined Cowichan knit round out the lineup NEEDLES is teaming up with Pendleton for the first time, debuting a six-piece NEEDLES x Pendleton collection that reworks the American mill’s classic plaids and wool cloth. Every garment starts from Pendleton’s fabric vocabulary, then gets recut through NEEDLES’ lens across shirting, tailoring, trousers and knits. The result is a tight capsule where the textiles do the talking and the construction choices tell you how each piece is meant to be worn.The shirt sets the foundation for the collection with a relaxed, boxy silhouette that gives the plaid wool room to drape rather than cling. That easy cut turns a traditional flannel-weight top into something closer to a light overshirt, built for layering through the colder months. The jacket builds on the same fabric language but adds leather patches at the elbows, a reinforcement detail that nods to hard-wearing workwear and protects one of the first areas to wear through on a wool garment.The coat is the statement piece of the drop, cut from a pattern pulled directly from Pendleton’s archive. Pairing that historical print with a full-length outer layer gives the design the most surface area to show off, making it the clearest showcase of the partnership’s archival focus. Plaid trousers complete the tailoring side, carrying the check pattern from top to bottom so the pieces can be worn as a coordinated set or broken up across a look.The knitwear leans into texture and structure. Pendleton’s staple Native-inspired pattern appears on a sweater knit with mohair, which brings a soft, slightly brushed hand and extra warmth to the fiber…

a4977d3fa4:5655c11cc962f0e0.title: The Nike Air Max 90 “Light Orewood Brown” Is All Patent Shine and See-Through Panels
a4977d3fa4:5655c11cc962f0e0.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:5655c11cc962f0e0.summary: Name: Nike Air Max 90 “Light Orewood Brown”Colorway: Light Orewood Brown/Blue Tint-Sail-Neutral OliveSKU: IX8056-104MSRP: $145 USDRelease Date: November 1Where to Buy: NikeNike is giving the Air Max 90 a material-driven makeover with the “Light Orewood Brown” colorway, pairing translucent overlays with high-gloss patent leather. The palette stays deliberately muted, sticking mostly to Light Orewood Brown and Sail so that texture and transparency become the main event. The result is a quiet take on Tinker Hatfield’s runner that rewards a closer look.The upper is built in layers that play off one another. Textured mesh forms the base across the toe box and collar, while translucent panels sweep along the sidewalls and frame the lacing system, letting the mesh show through from beneath. Down low, the mudguards are finished in glossy beige patent leather, adding shine and contrast without breaking from the tonal color scheme.Nike carries the see-through concept into the branding as well. The tongue labels and heel tabs are rendered in the same clear material, so the logos underneath remain visible through a glassy top layer. Cream laces and a matching lining keep the interior and lacing in step with the exterior, while a tonal midsole houses the silhouette’s signature visible Air unit in the heel.Underfoot, a semi-translucent outsole continues the theme from top to bottom. The standout accessory is a metallic Swoosh hangtag clipped to the laces, engraved with an intricate pattern that is echoed on the printed insoles. That artwork links the pair to a wider set of releases, with forthcoming Air Max 95 and Air Force 1 styles set to carry the same engraved motif alongside their own patent leather and translucent details. a4977d3fa4:dd10588e7fa335f2.title: White Mountaineering x Alpha Industries Splice Three Military Classics Into Two Hybrid Jackets
a4977d3fa4:dd10588e7fa335f2.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:dd10588e7fa335f2.summary: Summary White Mountaineering and ALPHA INDUSTRIES return for a third collaboration, built around two military-derived outerwear stylesA hybrid coat starts from the N-3B and borrows details from the MA-1 and CWU-45P, while a hybrid flight jacket pairs an MA-1 silhouette with N-3B elementsBoth styles combine water-repellent, high-density shells with a breathable, windproof WINDSTOPPER lining White Mountaineering and Alpha Industries have reunited for their third collaboration, a two-piece outerwear release that blends the American military outfitter’s archive with the Japanese label’s functional design. Rather than reissuing a single classic, each jacket mixes elements from several military flight and cold-weather styles into one hybrid build.The hybrid coat takes the N-3B as its foundation, keeping the longer, cold-weather proportions of the original while adding details drawn from both the MA-1 and the CWU-45P. Combining three distinct references in one garment gives the coat a familiar military feel without tying it to any single archival piece.The hybrid flight jacket works the same idea in reverse. It keeps the shorter, instantly recognizable silhouette of the MA-1 and layers in details from the N-3B, bringing some of the parka’s practicality into a more compact flight-jacket shape.Both styles share the same technical foundation. Each is cut from a densely woven fabric treated with a water-repellent finish to handle wet conditions, while the interior is lined with WINDSTOPPER, a membrane that blocks wind while letting moisture escape. That pairing allows both jackets to protect against the elements without trapping heat and sweat inside.The White Mountaineering x Alpha Industries collaboration drops October 31 via White Mountaineering stores, the White Mountaineering online store and select stockists across Japan. a4977d3fa4:21ef6e8935ad6eca.title: Better World Fragrance House and OVO Celebrate Drake’s 40th Birthday With "DoSayDo" Eau De Parfum
a4977d3fa4:21ef6e8935ad6eca.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:21ef6e8935ad6eca.summary: Summary Better World Fragrance House has partnered with October's Very Own for an exclusive fragrance launch celebrating Drake's birthdayThe DoSayDo Eau de Parfum arrives in a reimagined translucent crimson glass sphere bottle with a matching sculptural standThe citrus aromatic scent layers top notes of passion fruit and cannabis over a base of cognac white cedarwood and roasted tonka Better World Fragrance House and Drake's lifestyle brand October's Very Own have officially presented the collaborative "DoSayDo" Eau De Parfum. Arriving during a prolific year where the artist has released three albums and teased a fourth, the exclusive fragrance launch celebrates Drake’s 40th birthday across a customized 3.4 oz. (100 mL) vessel.The DoSayDo fragrance delivers a citrus aromatic profile engineered with contrasting notes that subtly pay homage to the artist. The scent opens with top notes of passionfruit, white wine spritz, cannabis, and clary sage oil, moving into a heart of petitgrain, black pepper oil, and rose oil. As the fragrance deepens, warm base notes of cognac, white cedarwood, and roasted tonka unfold into a rich finish.Packaging elevates BWFH's signature primary design into an all-glass construction, casting the iconic globe bottle and sculptural stand in a deep burgundy, translucent crimson shade. The secondary packaging features OVO's recognizable cream-colored carton, displaying the signature October's Very Own owl logo alongside the circular Better World Fragrance House emblem.The Better World Fragrance House x OVO DoSayDo Eau De Parfum previews via a 24-hour DTC release on October 19, 2026, at BetterWorldFragranceHouse followed by an official launch on October 24, 2026, in OVO stores and at OctobersVeryOwn. a4977d3fa4:0d938af9daaf6dcb.title: A. Lange & Söhne Marks 20 Years of the Datograph Perpetual in Platinum
a4977d3fa4:0d938af9daaf6dcb.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:0d938af9daaf6dcb.summary: Summary A. Lange & Söhne marks 20 years of the Datograph Perpetual with a new platinum edition.The black dial features 11 baguette-cut diamond hour markers.Its hand-wound L952.1 calibre combines flyback chronograph and perpetual calendar functions. To celebrate the 20th anniversary of the Datograph Perpetual, A. Lange & Söhne has introduced a highly exclusive 50-piece limited-edition update to the iconic grand complication model. First launched in 2006, the Datograph Perpetual was the brand's first wristwatch to seamlessly integrate a classic column-wheel flyback chronograph with a mechanical perpetual calendar and an outsize date.This new iteration elevates the original design by pairing a 41mm 950 platinum case and matching platinum bracelet with a striking black and rhodié-colored 925 silver dial. Further enhancing its prestige, the dial features eleven manually applied baguette-cut diamonds serving as hour markers, omitting indices at 4 and 8 o’clock to accommodate the prominent rhodié auxiliary dials.The dial is anchored by the signature Lange outsize date at 12 o'clock, which forms the tip of an equilateral triangle with the two main subdials. The subdial at 9 o'clock tracks small seconds, the day of the week, and a day/night indicator, while the 3 o'clock subdial displays the jumping minute counter, the month, and the leap-year cycle. A precise moon-phase display sits at 6 o'clock, completing the triangle.The perpetual calendar mechanism is programmed to remain accurate until March 2100, while the moon phase will deviate by a single day only after 122.6 years of continuous operation. Adjusting these displays is remarkably simple, utilizing a single rapid-correction pusher at 10 o'clock or individual recessed correctors.Driving these dual complications is the meticulously crafted L952.1 manually wound manufacture caliber, visible through a sapphire-crystal caseback. a4977d3fa4:f8b2f64699ad4751.title: Matt Hui's SS27 “Live to the Fullest” Collection Reimagines the Uniforms of Childhood
a4977d3fa4:f8b2f64699ad4751.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:f8b2f64699ad4751.summary: Summary Matt Hui's SS27 “Live to the Fullest” collection explores childhood nostalgia, freedom and self-discovery.School uniforms, scout attire and workwear inspire reconstructed tailoring, delicate knitwear and floral embellishments.A dreamlike campaign explores identity through playful contrasts between reality and illusion. What if growing up didn't mean leaving behind the freedom and fearlessness of childhood? Hong Kong-based designer Matt Hui explores this question through his Spring/Summer 2027 collection, “Live to the Fullest,” a nostalgic yet forward-looking study of identity, self-expression and the possibilities of rediscovering one's younger self.Following his debut collection, which drew from old family photographs and childhood drawings, Hui continues his introspective approach by revisiting the uniforms and everyday clothing that shaped his formative years. School uniforms, physical education kits, scout attire, workwear and even pajamas become the starting points for a wardrobe that challenges the boundaries between discipline and individuality. Hui reinterprets these underlying codes through unexpected proportions, softened tailoring and playful construction, exploring how the conventions of adulthood might coexist with the uninhibited spirit of youth.Throughout the range, traditional wardrobe elements are reconstructed into unconventional yet understated silhouettes. Scarves and ties are incorporated directly into garments, transforming accessories typically associated with formal dressing into integral design features. Classic pinstripes recur across the lineup, referencing the rigidity of uniforms while taking on a more relaxed, contemporary character. Hui balances structured tailoring with lightweight cotton lawn, soft cotton jersey, paper yarn and fine cashmere, introducing tactile contrasts that lend the pieces an effortless, lived-in quality.Delicate floral embroidery, pointelle lace knitting and fully fashioned construction further soften…

a4977d3fa4:2f9dbe413561d987.title: Maison Margiela Celebrates 20 Years of Its Ebisu Tokyo Store With New "Folders" Chapter
a4977d3fa4:2f9dbe413561d987.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:2f9dbe413561d987.summary: Summary Maison Margiela has introduced a new chapter of its documentation project titled Maison Margiela/folders to honor 20 years of its Ebisu Tokyo flagshipThe project highlights the building's evolution from a former electrical products factory alongside interviews with local Tabi collectors and original staffThe rollout includes a limited-edition zine and an in-store Line 2 cultural dialogue installation open to the public from November 5 to November 15 Maison Margiela has officially unveiled a new chapter of MaisonMargiela/folders, celebrating 20 years at its foundational Tokyo boutique located at 2-8-13 Ebisu Minami.In September 2000, 12 years into the house's history, the brand opened its first-ever standalone store not in Paris or Belgium, but in a traditional residential home in the Tokyo suburb of Ebisu at 3-3-3 Ebisu Minami. When required to relocate in 2006, the label avoided commercial strips and instead deepened its commitment to the neighborhood by acquiring a former electrical products factory just five minutes away at 2-8-13 Ebisu Minami. Retaining team members who have worked at the location since its inception, the space has served as the physical anchor for the brand's identity and creative milestones in Japan for the past two decades.Titled "Maison Margiela Tokyo: 20 Years at 2-8-13," the documentation project records oral histories from staff, investigates the district's creative landscape, and spotlights the local community of Tabi collectors. Alongside the historical survey, the initiative documents "Line 2: Unravelled Memory, Rewoven Future," which captures a cross-cultural collaboration between Japanese artist Mio Suzuki and French tapestry fabricators Les Manufactures Nationales – Sèvres & Mobilier National.The initial archive preview is accessible now via the Maison Margiela website, while the physical limited-edition ZINE will distribute across Ebisu on November 5 alongside the Line 2 installation, which remains on view in-store…

a4977d3fa4:8bfda4078f8460e2.title: Marmot x CITY COUNTRY CITY’s “Everywhere” Capsule Layers Up for Winter
a4977d3fa4:8bfda4078f8460e2.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)

a4977d3fa4:4594318298a3a526.summary: YOKE has officially presented its Fall/Winter 2026 collection, titled "Beyond Form," alongside the announcement of its first international pop-up space at BELOWGROUND in Hong Kong.Founded in 2018 by designer Norio Terada, YOKE derives its name from the tailoring term for the pattern piece that connects and joins fabric together, framing the brand's core ethos: “Things connect people, people connect people, and people connect things.” For the FW26 season, the Tokyo Fashion Award-winning designer channels his background in fine art to merge sculpture with daily wear, drawing heavily from the surrealist work of Jean Arp.Guided by Arp’s philosophy that “nature knows no straight lines,” the collection departs from rigid structures in favor of organic contours and accidental form. Classic garments receive subtle, rounded proportions, while trench coats incorporate internal wiring that allows wearers to freely sculpt and manipulate the silhouette. Surrealist techniques also manifest through fabric bonding on glen check overcoats, capturing the visual state of loosely and casually positioned cloth. To translate this tactile concept to the runway during its Paris presentation, Terada placed self-crafted ceramics on venue seats, encouraging guests to touch the organic curves and experience the materials firsthand.Marking a major milestone in the brand's global presence, YOKE is bringing the collection to Hong Kong for its first international pop-up in collaboration with Gallery HBX. How did it directly inspire this…

a4977d3fa4:758b1697cff743a3.title: 8 Must-See Shows in Paris Right Now
a4977d3fa4:758b1697cff743a3.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:758b1697cff743a3.summary: The Grand Palais alone isn’t enough to contain Art Basel Paris. One of the art world’s most anticipated weeks, each year the event, now in its fifth edition, gives life to new perspectives and possibilities, be it at the fair floor, satellite shows, or overheards at the afters.But this year’s edition feels especially urgent. Protests over education cuts and the rising cost of living have left several fairs, museums, and galleries to scale back their weekend programming. While this means an abrupt end to the main event, it’s also a wake-up to the reality of living, a subject that, for centuries, artists never feared to confront. ⁠What’s happening outside the white cube is defining our look inside of it. From new ways of seeing, ancestral histories, and trips through Paris’ own protest history, we’ve rounded up a list of must-see satellite moments, many of which are up through next year. Artists have always had a way with capturing the world, and in these shows, they’re not just facing, but imagining it anew. ⁠Jenny Holzer’s ‘J’ai Vu’ at Musée d’OrsayOn view until February 21, 2027.There’s no one "right place" for Jenny Holzer’s texts. From the streets to the world’s most esteemed museums, the conceptual artist has spent decades turning art into tools of confrontation. At Musée d’Orsay, Holzer pulls from the museum’s own archives, putting yesterday’s writings into monumental LED installations, projects, stone sculptures, and metal paintings into conversation with today’s conflicts and contradictions.Barbara Kruger’s ‘The History of Tears’ at Bourse de CommerceOn view until January 25, 2027.Barbara Kruger’s massive Bourse de Commerce commission sizes up to both her own artistic imprint and ceaseless exploration of visual systems that rule us. Streams of text, video, and collage pour through the rotunda, bringing issues of power, sexuality, and alienation to light. Highlights include “Power, Pleasure, Desire, Disgust,” her 1996 video work that inaugurated Jeffrey…

a4977d3fa4:f65439ce12c58f45.title: Meet Alba, Milan’s New Approach to Golf Apparel
a4977d3fa4:f65439ce12c58f45.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:f65439ce12c58f45.summary: Most new golf brands introduce themselves online. They build an Instagram following, share a visual world and, eventually, show the product. Alba took a different route. After years of development largely out of public view, the Milan-based label made its first impression in person: a tournament at Circolo Golf Villa d'Este, hosted in collaboration with Porsche Italy.The setting instantly communicated its intent. Founded in 1926, Villa d'Este is among Italy's oldest golf clubs, with a history that gives the occasion a sense of importance before anyone reaches the bag drop. And for a brand's first event, it was an ambitious introduction. Porsche's involvement, meanwhile, suggested that Alba had already built relationships well beyond the usual circle of emerging golf labels.Coming from Milan brings its own expectations. A golf brand from a city so closely associated with fashion invites scrutiny of its fabrics, construction and overall aesthetic. Alba seemed prepared for that. The collection shown at Villa d'Este felt considered from the start, with an attention to material and finish that can take younger brands years to develop.Its appeal lies in the relationship between refined clothing and equipment made to play in. Some pieces had the natural hand feel and restraint you might expect from an Italian fashion label. Elsewhere, nylon, concealed zippers and seam-sealed outerwear made the functional intent clear. Alba also drew on production expertise close to home and sourced fabrics farther away, including Scotland. The result was understated, but it wasn't an absence of ideas disguised as minimalism.The guest list reflected a similarly refined approach. Milanese watchmakers played alongside brand executives, designers and agency founders. Fabio Fognini was there, as were visitors from the UK and France, including people connected to Pluto of St Andrews and Palace Skateboards. It was a gathering of golfers and people whose work touches fashion, design and culture,…

a4977d3fa4:2c9bee1706868741.title: Hypeart Visits: Yichen Ji on the Human Side of Technology
a4977d3fa4:2c9bee1706868741.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:2c9bee1706868741.summary: For Yichen Ji, technology is more than a tool for making art. It's a way to explore how we experience the world, connect with one another and make sense of things that don't always have clear answers.Raised in Shanghai and now based in New York, Ji works across digital media, sculpture, installation and printmaking, often bringing computational processes into conversation with traditional materials. His work moves between the familiar and the futuristic, finding unexpected ways to make abstract ideas feel tangible.In "Synthetic Genesis," visitors can pick up a futuristic payphone and speak with more than 100,000 fictional AI personas, each with their own identity and personality. His "Lattice" series takes crystalline structures that could never exist in the physical world and gives them new life through silkscreen printing. Meanwhile, "Chaos Clock" turns the simple act of telling time into something unpredictable, reflecting his own experience of living with ADHD.Across these projects, Ji is less concerned with celebrating technology or warning against it than with understanding what happens when it becomes part of our everyday lives.For this edition of our Visits series, we caught up with Ji to talk about growing up between two fast-moving cities, why he finds beauty in the friction between digital and handmade processes, and what he's messing with next."The push and pull between the polished and the raw, the digital and the physical, comes a lot from living in both."Your practice moves between digital media, sculpture, installation and printmaking. How do you decide what form an idea ultimately takes?Honestly, I let the idea tell me. I usually start with a question or a feeling rather than a medium, and then I ask myself what the viewer actually needs to do to understand it. If the idea is about perception or the passage of time, it probably needs to be physical and interactive, something you have to move around to complete. If it's about images, systems, or…

a4977d3fa4:8fc620c3e3b0746d.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:8fc620c3e3b0746d.summary: Summary Apple Original Films has revealed the title of its Fleetwood Mac documentary, the first ever made with the band’s full authorizationThe film gathers the perspectives of Mick Fleetwood, John McVie, Christine McVie, Lindsey Buckingham and Stevie Nicks across more than five decadesIts premiere lines up with the 50th anniversary of Rumors, the album that gave the documentary its name Apple Original Films has officially titled its Fleetwood Mac documentary Fleetwood Mac: The Chain, marking the first time the band has signed off on a film telling its story from the inside. Directed by Frank Marshall, the project centers the five members of the band’s best-known lineup and is set for a global debut on Apple TV early next year.The documentary is built around the band itself rather than outside commentators. Mick Fleetwood, John McVie, Christine McVie, Lindsey Buckingham and Stevie Nicks, all Grammy winners and Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inductees, look back on the 50-plus years that followed their chance meeting in 1974. Archival material that has never been made public sits alongside exclusive new interviews, carrying the story from their record-breaking studio sessions and tours up to the present day.The title is a deliberate choice. “The Chain” is the only track on Rumors that credits all five members as writers, and the film uses it as a symbol for a bond that held even as the band’s rise to fame strained nearly every relationship within it. Timing reinforces the point, with the premiere landing on the 50th anniversary of the Grammy-winning album’s release.Structurally, the film moves through the band’s peaks and collapses while isolating what each member contributed to a sound that has sold more than 220 million records worldwide. It also digs into the harder question of why five artists kept returning to one another, and kept producing landmark work, despite pressures from the industry and from within the group that repeatedly threatened to end it.Behind the…

a4977d3fa4:f22cb48f60a07516.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:f22cb48f60a07516.summary: Summary Amazon MGM Studios is reportedly beginning final screen tests to cast the next James BondAuditions are being overseen by casting director Nina Gold for director Denis VilleneuveCallum Turner and Jack Lowden have emerged among the names in the mix as an official announcement looms before year's end Amazon MGM Studios is officially entering the final stages of casting for the next James Bond. Final screen tests to determine the new 007 are slated to commence within the coming week, starting as early as Friday.While the complete roster of actors invited to audition remains unconfirmed, industry sources note that British stars Callum Turner and Jack Lowden are actively in the mix. Representatives for Turner, Lowden, and Amazon MGM Studios did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Acclaimed filmmaker Denis Villeneuve is attached to direct the franchise's upcoming chapter, with veteran casting director Nina Gold managing the extensive audition process.Both frontrunners have circulated throughout the franchise's rumor mill in recent months. Lowden gained notable traction after his Slow Horses co-star Gary Oldman publicly hinted that the Scottish actor had reached the studio shortlist. Addressing the ongoing chatter, Lowden’s wife, Saoirse Ronan, downplayed the domestic speculation, noting that it’s “not really a subject that’s coming up in our house.” Turner similarly addressed 007 inquiries while promoting the arthouse film Rosebush Pruning at the Berlin Film Festival earlier this year. “It’s very early for that question,” Turner remarked at the time. “I’m not going to comment on it.”While Amazon MGM Studios has not announced a specific date for the formal reveal, the studio is widely expected to name its next James Bond before the end of the year. a4977d3fa4:f85c3b0170636d93.title: Chris Pratt Confirms Star-Lord Will Return to the MCU

a4977d3fa4:f85c3b0170636d93.summary: Summary Chris Pratt has confirmed that Star-Lord will return to the Marvel Cinematic UniverseThe actor revealed on The Playlist’s Bingeworthy podcast that hard action has been taken by Marvel Studios leadershipPratt previously pitched his own creative vision to Kevin Feige to help shape future MCU storytelling Marvel Studios and actor Chris Pratt are officially moving forward with Star-Lord's return to the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Pratt confirmed on The Playlist’s “Bingeworthy” podcast that concrete steps have been initiated to follow up on the character’s future teased at the close of Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3.Speaking on the podcast, Pratt addressed his ongoing communication with executive leadership regarding Peter Quill's return, "I have a great relationship with Kevin [Feige] and Lou [D’Esposito], and there have been both ongoing conversations about how we make good on that promise and also hard action taken to make sure that we make good on that promise," said Pratt. He continued, "So yeah, you’ll see Star-Lord again, which is very exciting, but I’m not at liberty to say when that’s going to be, but he’s not going anywhere."The confirmation builds upon statements Pratt made earlier on the Happy Sad Confused podcast, where he admitted to pitching a concept directly to Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige. “I’m happy to do anything they want me to do and will,” Pratt previously explained. “And also, I personally have a really strong vision of what I would want him to do. And I think it’s fucking great.” When asked about bringing that proposal to Feige, Pratt stated, “Yep. And I think that, you know, I’m down to contribute any way I can to them setting up the next 10 years of storytelling, you know? a4977d3fa4:2b0a076da2e4b7c1.title: ARC’TERYX’s Postour Boot Hides a Slipper Inside a GORE-TEX Shell
a4977d3fa4:2b0a076da2e4b7c1.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:2b0a076da2e4b7c1.summary: Name: ARC’TERYX Postour Boot Men'sColorway: Black/Black, Tatsu/BlackSKU: X000010507MSRP: $300 USDRelease Date: Available nowWhere to Buy: ARC’TERYXARC’TERYX is targeting the downtime between backcountry days with the Postour Boot, a two-part recovery boot built for après touring. An insulated, waterproof overboot handles snow and ice outdoors, while a separate slipper slides out from inside so wearers can head straight indoors without swapping footwear.The overboot is the weatherproof half of the system. ARC’TERYX wraps it in GORE-TEX Invisible Fit, running the waterproof layer all the way up to the top of the collar for extra protection and warmth. That high collar closes with a drawcord that tightens much like a climbing chalk bag, sealing the opening against deep snow and slush. Endure 360 extended rubber coverage circles the entire boot, reinforcing it against scuffs and impacts.Grip comes from a Vibram Arctic Grip outsole engineered for secure footing on icy ground, paired with a lug pattern shaped to bite into snow and other soft terrain. Underfoot cushioning adds a layer of comfort for feet that have spent the day locked into stiff ski boots.Warmth runs through both layers. Coreloft synthetic insulation lines the overboot and the slipper, so the pair stays warm whether it’s worn as a full boot outside or reduced to the inner piece indoors. The slipper itself is fully functional on its own, offering support when nested inside the boot and switching to a TPU grip outsole made for indoor surfaces once it’s pulled out.The men’s Postour comes in two colorways, Black/Black and Tatsu/Black, both built with a textile upper, synthetic insole and rubber outsole, and listed for alpine, touring, freeride and resort use. ARC’TERYX notes the boot is PFAS compliant and requires surface cleaning only. Sizing runs in whole sizes, and the brand recommends sizing up for anyone between sizes or after a roomier fit. a4977d3fa4:32aa9c044ebee299.title: LISA’s ‘PRESS PLAY’ EP Plays Out Like a Six-Track Action Movie

The project arrives today alongside a music video for focus track “Tarantino,” capping a run that has already delivered a record-breaking YouTube debut, a historic VMA win and a sold-out Las Vegas booking.The film framing shapes how the EP is sequenced, with six tracks moving like scenes rather than a loose collection of singles. “SaWaDiKa” opens the reel, followed by “V12” and “Cobra,” before “Tarantino” lands as the centerpiece and “Cut U Off” and “Sweat” carry things to the closing credits.“Tarantino” gets the blockbuster treatment on screen. Its video follows LISA on a mission through a hotel to hand-deliver a note to the director himself, throwing punches at anyone standing between her and the delivery. The action-heavy choreography leans straight into the genre the track is named after, making it the clearest visual statement of the EP’s movie concept.The project’s opener already arrived with serious numbers. “SaWaDiKa,” named after the Thai greeting for “hello,” came with a video shot in LISA’s hometown of Bangkok that pulled in more than 70.8 million YouTube views in its first 24 hours. a4977d3fa4:7d2e1fcc3072f878.title: Denzel Washington and Christopher McQuarrie Set to Team up for Untitled Amazon MGM Thriller
a4977d3fa4:7d2e1fcc3072f878.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:7d2e1fcc3072f878.summary: Summary Denzel Washington is set to headline an untitled original thriller directed by Christopher McQuarrieAmazon MGM and United Artists have slated the feature for an October 1, 2027 theatrical releaseWritten by Scott Barkan and Gregg Zehentner the plot centers on a terminally ill ex-detective confronting his past Amazon MGM Studios and United Artists have officially greenlit an untitled original thriller starring two-time Academy Award winner Denzel Washington and directed by Christopher McQuarrie. The high-profile feature is currently slated to arrive in theaters in the fall of 2027.Penned by screenwriters Scott Barkan and Gregg Zehentner, the project—previously developed under the working title The Frame—focuses on a former police detective who receives an early release from prison following a terminal brain cancer diagnosis. Hoping to spend his remaining time reconnecting with his family, he quickly discovers that his unresolved past refuses to stay buried.The collaboration with McQuarrie marks one of two major Washington-led productions scheduled for the near future. The actor was previously set to debut The Take—originally titled Here Comes the Flood and co-starring Robert Pattinson—before the end of 2026, though that production has since seen its release window pushed into 2027.The untitled Christopher McQuarrie thriller starring Denzel Washington is scheduled for a theatrical rollout on October 1, 2027. a4977d3fa4:f4e2d688226ce7b0.title: The Nike Air Force 1 ‘01 “Philly” Gives LeBron James a Sixers-Coded Welcome
a4977d3fa4:f4e2d688226ce7b0.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:f4e2d688226ce7b0.summary: Name: Nike Air Force 1 ’01 “Philly”Colorway: White/Rush Blue-University RedSKU: JW9694-100MSRP: $140 USDRelease Date: Available nowWhere to Buy: SNKRSNike is greeting LeBron James’ move to Philadelphia with the Air Force 1 ‘01 “Philly,” a city-dedicated pair dressed in Sixers colors and loaded with local references. Rather than a signature-line release, the brand is leaning on its most recognizable low-top to mark the moment, building the shoe around Philadelphia itself.This is the second time in 2026 that Nike has turned the Air Force 1 ‘01 into a snapshot of a city’s basketball mood. Earlier this year, the “NYC” edition arrived as the Knicks pushed through the playoffs, its insoles printed with a pixelated rendering of Madison Square Garden. The “Philly” pair trades arena imagery for team colors and civic shorthand, keeping the tribute rooted in the city rather than a single building.Up top, the White/Rush Blue-University Red colorway is mapped with clear intent. White leather handles the toe, lacing area and heel, while royal blue covers the perforated toe box and side panels. Red leather Swooshes sweep across each side, and a smaller red Swoosh sits just below the laces to carry the accent color toward the center of the shoe.The heel is where the city really announces itself. One shoe is embroidered with “215” and the other with “PHL,” each outlined in blue and cut through by a red Swoosh, while white “Phila” lettering stands in for standard branding on the blue heel tabs. “215” is one of Philadelphia’s area codes, giving the pair a local detail only the city would fully read.Underfoot, a white midsole carries blue “AIR” lettering and sits on a blue rubber outsole. The most pointed detail hides inside: the insoles show a black-and-white brick wall split by cracks, with a red Nike logo smashing through one section. For a shoe built around a star landing in a new city, it’s a fitting image to stand on. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Reimagined through a contemporary leisure lens, this modern release retains its classic court foundation while upgrading its construction with refined, tactile materials.Replacing the silhouette's traditional canvas uppers, the design incorporates a contrasting blend of hairy suede and crocodile-stamped leather for added texture and polish. The low-profile uppers sit atop a distinct gum midsole, introducing an understated nod to 1980s athletic engineering over traditional vulcanized sole units. Offered in two distinct colorways—"Espresso" and "Milk"—the palette draws direct aesthetic cues from the warmth, textures, and canine visitors of local neighborhood coffee shops.The Todd Snyder x New Balance T500 “Cafe Pack” releases October 22 at 10 AM ET for $130 USD, available exclusively at online and all Todd Snyder retail locations. a4977d3fa4:0fe0914121df85c6.summary: Devialet officially unveils the all-new Phantom Ultimate 98 dB "Pulse Blue" Collector's Edition speaker. a4977d3fa4:59f19d42bbbc554a.title: A-POC ABLE ISSEY MIYAKE x JAXA Turn Satellite Shots of Antarctic Ice Into “TYPE-XVII” Jeans
a4977d3fa4:59f19d42bbbc554a.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:59f19d42bbbc554a.summary: Summary A-POC ABLE ISSEY MIYAKE has teamed up with the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency on new jeans under its “TYPE-XVII JAXA project”The design pulls from Antarctic observation images captured by JAXA’s climate change monitoring satellite “SHIKISAI”Wide and straight silhouettes are offered, each made with the label’s in-house single-cloth jacquard technique A-POC ABLE ISSEY MIYAKE is taking its textile engineering into orbit with the “TYPE-XVII JAXA project” jeans, a collaboration with the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). Instead of printing an image onto finished fabric, the pair translates satellite data of Earth directly into the weave, with Antarctica serving as the design’s focal point.The source material comes from “SHIKISAI,” the JAXA satellite tasked with observing climate change from above. Its images of the southern continent supply the entire visual language here: sweeping fields of white ice interrupted by fissures where dark navy ocean shows through. The result reads less like a graphic and more like a topographic surface you can wear.Construction is where the project earns its spec-sheet credibility. A-POC ABLE ISSEY MIYAKE renders the imagery through its proprietary jacquard, building each pair from one continuous piece of cloth so the Antarctic pattern lives inside the textile rather than sitting on top of it. That approach lets the contrast between ice and sea carry through the garment as part of its structure.Two silhouettes anchor the drop. A wide jean offers a roomier, relaxed leg, while a straight version keeps a cleaner line, and both arrive in a run of four sizes so the satellite-derived pattern can scale across different builds.The A-POC ABLE ISSEY MIYAKE x JAXA “TYPE-XVII JAXA project” jeans drop November 1 via A-POC ABLE ISSEY MIYAKE / AOYAMA, A-POC ABLE ISSEY MIYAKE / KYOTO and ISSEY MIYAKE GINZA / 442. a4977d3fa4:b63e363b077b353f.summary: Summary Florida rapper Doechii has released the latest installment of her Swamp Sessions series titled "CATWOMAN"The visual features the artist in dual roles as she wanders the desert before an explosive confrontationThe release builds momentum for the Grammy winner as she teases the creative direction of her upcoming debut album Top Dawg Entertainment artist Doechii has officially released "CATWOMAN," the latest explosive visual installment in her ongoing Swamp Sessions series. The music video arrived on Tuesday, October 20, following the release of last week's thunderous single "BOMBS."In the new video, the Swamp Princess wanders through a desert landscape wearing baggy washed denim jeans, a Tap Out waistband, and a white sports bra before being blown to pieces by a bazooka-wielding, alternate version of herself. Rocking an Afro, black denim, heels, and matching sunglasses, this second persona struts to the scene while delivering hard-hitting bars. a4977d3fa4:5db055a342db93b4.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:5db055a342db93b4.summary: Summary A Florida bankruptcy court has confirmed the sale of Dame Dash’s life rights to Everlasting Films LLC for $550,000 USDThe acquisition secures exclusive worldwide rights to his narrative alongside 100 hours of video footage memorabilia and an in-development film projectBackup bidder Doug Peters is positioned to purchase the rights for 500,000 USD if the primary sale fails to close Dame Dash has officially seen his Life Rights auctioned off for $550,000 USD, with all proceeds allocated directly to satisfy his creditors. The conclusion of the auction was formally submitted by bankruptcy trustee Traci K. Stevenson to the overseeing Florida court on Wednesday, October 21.Following the bidding process that concluded on October 1, Everlasting Films, LLC—which originally submitted an initial $37,000 USD “stalking horse” bid—won the auction to secure exclusive worldwide rights to the Roc-A-Fella co-founder's life story. Alongside narrative rights, the sale includes “100 hours of video content, photographs, and memorabilia,” as well as “an unreleased, in-development documentary/film project.” In the event that Everlasting Films does not finalize the deal within the required window, backup bidder Doug Peters is queued to claim the rights for $500,000 USD.The auction stems from a petition filed by Stevenson in August after Dash declared bankruptcy in September 2025, listing $25 million USD in liabilities against $4,350 USD in personal assets. While Dash omitted the asset in his initial filing, Stevenson argued the rights held “evident value in light of the Debtor's public profile and his historical association with Roc-A-Fella Records and [Jay-Z].” Elaborating on the commercial valuation, Stevenson wrote, "[T]he monetization of an individual's name, image, and likeness has become a well-established and actively regulated commercial market. a4977d3fa4:caf6c4c04639d1b7.summary: Summary Zane Li of ready-to-wear label Lii has been awarded the 2026 CFDA/Vogue Fashion FundThe designer takes home a 300,000 USD prize alongside comprehensive business mentorshipRunners-up Emily Dawn Long and Aisling Camps each received 100,000 USD at the celebratory dinner in New York The CFDA and Vogue have officially crowned Zane Li of Lii as the winner of the 2026 CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund. The announcement arrived during a celebratory dinner at The Crane Club in New York, co-hosted by Tory Burch, Thom Browne, Chloe Malle, and Anna Wintour.Li, a Chongqing-born, New York-based FIT graduate whose label explores the intersection of sport and couture, takes home a $300,000 USD grant alongside dedicated business mentorship. The honor marks the culmination of a breakout year for the designer, who previously won the Fashion Trust U.S. Ready-to-Wear award and took home the Karl Lagerfeld Prize at the LVMH Prize ceremony in Paris last month.Runners-up Emily Dawn Long and Aisling Camps each received $100,000 USD. The remaining finalists in this year’s pool included Amir Taghi, Terrence Zhou (Bad Binch TongTong), Jamie Haller, Julia Ferentinos (Juju Vera), George Inaki (Milamore), Claire Sullivan (Miss Claire Sullivan), and Zoe Gustavia Anna Whalen.Reflecting on the class of designers, CFDA Chairman Thom Browne noted: “The CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund is an important reminder of why we must continue to champion original voices and true creativity….Each of this year’s finalists bring a distinct point of view that only they could….Their true individuality is what makes American fashion so compelling and supporting their future is the responsibility of our industry….I look forward to seeing what they do next.” Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:5b78ea77e3cc2465.title: Shanghai Grand Opera House Opens With Snøhetta’s Sweeping Waterfront Design
a4977d3fa4:5b78ea77e3cc2465.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:5b78ea77e3cc2465.summary: Summary Snøhetta’s Shanghai Grand Opera House opens along the Huangpu River.A sweeping roof doubles as a public staircase and panoramic viewing platform.Three performance venues anchor the 146,786-square-meter cultural complex. Shanghai’s waterfront has gained a new cultural landmark with the opening of the Shanghai Grand Opera House, designed by Snøhetta in collaboration with East China Architectural Design & Research Institute, Theatre Projects and Nagata Acoustics.Located in the Expo Houtan district along the Huangpu River, the 146,786-square-meter complex is defined by a sweeping white roof that folds upward into a spiraling public staircase, turning the building itself into an extension of the surrounding cityscape. Snøhetta designed its circulation as part of the public realm, allowing visitors to move from ground level to a rooftop observation deck with panoramic views of the river and Shanghai skyline. Expansive glazing, landscaped connections and open gathering spaces further soften the building’s monumental scale, giving the predominantly white exterior a light, civic character.Inside, the opera house accommodates 4,200 spectators across three distinct performance spaces: the 2,000-seat Harmony Hall, the 1,200-seat Soar Theatre and the adaptable 1,000-seat Open Stage, alongside rehearsal, production, exhibition, educational and hospitality facilities. Each auditorium develops its own identity, with Harmony Hall contrasting the restrained exterior through deep red tones and sculptural surfaces shaped around the acoustic demands of opera.Restaurants, exhibitions and public spaces extend activity beyond scheduled performances, reinforcing the building’s role as an everyday cultural destination rather than a venue used solely for events. Selected through an international competition in 2016, the decade-long project officially opened, alongside the launch of its inaugural Born to Sing season and the opening of the 25th China Shanghai International Arts…

a4977d3fa4:54d9bc9bd3615c60.title: 7-Eleven Drops Trademark Lawsuit Against Nike Over Air Max 95
a4977d3fa4:54d9bc9bd3615c60.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:54d9bc9bd3615c60.summary: Summary 7-Eleven has officially dropped its trademark lawsuit against Nike regarding the Air Max 95Court filings confirm the dismissal was accepted with prejudice meaning the convenience brand cannot sue on the same groundsNike has not confirmed an updated release date or whether the sneaker will officially launch at retail Looks like Nike may potentially release the Air Max 95 "7-Eleven" at retail after 7-Eleven officially dropped its lawsuit against the sportswear brand. According to the latest court documents, the legal dispute surrounding the contentious sneaker has now been formally dismissed.The legal conflict began in July 2026 when 7-Eleven filed a lawsuit to halt the rollout of the Air Max 95, claiming the shoe’s design mimicked its brand color scheme too closely. The company also sought to block a planned launch on July 11—nationally celebrated as 7-Eleven Day—arguing that consumers would mistakenly assume Nike was releasing an official collaboration with the brand.Court records from October 19 indicate that 7-Eleven moved to dismiss the lawsuit with prejudice, barring the retailer from bringing future legal action against Nike on the same grounds. The filing was officially accepted by the court on October 20, with both parties ordered to pay their own attorney costs. No public details have been disclosed explaining why the suit was dropped or whether an out-of-court settlement was reached.While the lawsuit attempted to stop the release, pairs leaked onto secondary platforms such as StockX, GOAT, and eBay prior to July, where they traded above retail prices. Nike has not announced a new release date or confirmed if the Air Max 95 "7-Eleven" will ever receive a public retail drop. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:1a23893da7c5bb86.summary: Summary Art Basel Paris has announced that it will close its 2026 edition early, ending on Friday, October 23, instead of Sunday, October 25, as initially plannedThe decision has been confirmed via emails to exhibitors and a public announcement, citing fears for visitors' safety as protests continue to erupt across the French capitalSeveral museums, galleries, and alternative fairs are also adjusting their schedules to account for upcoming protests Art Basel Paris is cutting its fifth edition short, shutting the fair after Friday, October 23. The fair told exhibitors that the decision is “in the interest of safeguarding our visitors,” in a recent email shared Wednesday afternoon, and comes amid concerns of protests unfolding across the French capital this weekend.The fifth edition, gathering 211 galleries, was set to run through Sunday, October 25 at the Grand Palais. Art Basel brought in additional security measures — concrete anti-ram barriers and 24-hour patrols — for VIP previews so far following a temporary lockdown during installation earlier this week. Public viewing and in-person programming now solely consists of Friday’s schedule.“We deeply regret that we will not be able to welcome visitors this weekend, and extend our sincere appreciation to our galleries, artists, partners, visitors, and wider community around our fair,” Art Basel wrote in an Instagram post.Several French platforms, labor unions, and advocacy groups whose work centers issues of censorship and labor conditions within France’s contemporary art scene issued calls for protests both outside and within the fair on Saturday.The Parisian art week coincides with one of the biggest protests the country has seen in years. Protests, some escalating into riots and looting, have erupted across the country in light of Macron government’s budget cuts to the French public schooling system. a4977d3fa4:3e23d9236d1010ce.title: Back Market’s Slow Tech Summit Made a Stand Against Upgrade Culture
a4977d3fa4:3e23d9236d1010ce.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:3e23d9236d1010ce.summary: When a typical smartphone is made, it needs approximately 266 kg of raw materials and produces 80% of its carbon footprint in the first minute it’s turned on. As well as having a number of environmental effects, extracting the materials also comes with ethical and geopolitical costs.This is where Back Market’s Slow Tech Summit comes in. Taking place in Paris last week, the one-day event aimed to explore how we can make devices last at least 10 years as an alternative to buying a new smartphone. Through a diverse programme, the refurbished tech marketplace welcomed journalists, scientists, activists, as well as designers, creators and athletes to understand the cost of new technology. Over the day, talks and debates were held with a line-up of industry experts: Back Market co-founder and executive chairman Thibaud Hug de Larauze; REEcover CEO Dr. Marie Perrin; Journalist Alice Pfeiffer; Génération Lumière founder David Maenda Kithoko; and journalist and author of Power Metal, Vince Beiser. Following discussions of extraction through their respective fields, Back Market CPO Amandine Durr also took the stage to share instant solutions for reusing tech with the announcement of Back Market Outlet.Offering a more hands-on approach to repair, several creators were on the ground with specially curated workshops. Italian analog archivist Davide Bonetti, better known as lecronachedidave, worked directly with repurposed technology in the Obsolescence as a Creative Tool masterclass, showing how these parts provide new possibilities in design, music and content creation with his magic TV. Delving deeper into the craft space, British creator Ube Boobey brought an imaginative lens to reclaimed components, guiding guests through a workshop in creating a cyber deck. The space was complete with a Slow Tech exhibition. Serving as a reminder of the harrowing cost of upgrades, it featured immersive images and displays that captured the environmental, geopolitical, and human impact of…

a4977d3fa4:056f3657a7087469.title: Kennedy Yanko Makes Paint and Metal-Bending a Devotional Act
a4977d3fa4:056f3657a7087469.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:056f3657a7087469.summary: Summary Miami-based artist Kennedy Yanko unveils a new solo exhibition, 'Ce qui nous rassemble,' in ParisThe show features a new body of sculptures made of found metal scraps and paint skins, exploring mysticism, sexuality, sacredness, and devotion through the act of creation Kennedy Yanko’s abstract sculptures are tense with history and possibility. Created from scrap metal parts wrapped with paint skins, each surface bears records of beauty and decay when shaped into luminous, veiled forms. Their histories aren’t erased, but transformed through the act of making, which makes Cité de l’Architecture et du Patrimoine in Paris an apt stage for her latest creations.The Miami-based artist debuts a new series of sculptures in Ce qui nous rassemble. Set amidst casts of architectural fragments from French churches and cathedrals, the show, which translates to “what brings us together,” explores creation as love, a devotional act that can both point back to the past and guide us through an age-old desire for transcendence.Devotion and agency thematically ground the presentation, interwoven with ideas of mysticism and gender. This particular body of work is by Mary Magdalene, one of Christianity’s most controversial figures. Here Yanko reimagines her story to consider the many labels she occupies in the cultural imaginary, while highlighting the distortion of feminine sexual power throughout religious history.It is unity, though, that persists. Yanko connects creation as a means of bodily agency — the desirer and desired — and through the act of material rupture and becoming, brings out the generative energies that bind us all. “She sees the human being in a similar way,” the exhibition text reads, “an energetic instrument whose capacity to create depends on intention, attention, and continual clearing and recalibration.”Ce qui nous rassemble is now on view in Paris until January 3, 2027, as part of Art Basel Paris’ public program.Cité de l’Architecture et du Patrimoine1…

a4977d3fa4:10243d6980ab8df9.title: Zane Li of LII Wins 2026 CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund
a4977d3fa4:10243d6980ab8df9.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:10243d6980ab8df9.summary: SummaryChongqing-born FIT graduate Zane Li won the CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund, earning $300,000 and mentorship for his label LII.Runners-up Aisling Camps and Emily Dawn Long each received $100,000.Chinese designer Zane Li of LII has been announced as the official winner of the CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund, with Aisling Camps and Emily Dawn Long as runners-up.Since stepping onto the NYC scene in 2024, the Chongqing-born designer and 2023 FIT graduate has quickly become renowned for his clean blend of sport styles with unconventional silhouettes and bold color. While maintaining a minimal ethos, the designer’s collections have spoken volumes in their stark color blocking and experimental cuts, garnering attention from industry leaders. The designer has already won the Karl Lagerfeld Prize at the LVMH Prize and the Fashion Trust US Ready-to-Wear Award this year. As the winner of the main prize, Li’s label will receive $300,000 USD, while runners-up Camps and Longs will receive a $100,000 USD grant. Furthermore, the fund’s monetary prizes are complemented with guided mentorship for the awardees. Other finalists from this year’s program included Amir Taghi, Terrence Zhou of Bad Binch Tongtong, Jamie Haller, Julia Ferentinos of Juju Vera, George Inaki of Milamore, Claire Sullivan of Miss Claire Sullivan, and Zoe Gustavia Anna Whalen. In previous years, the CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund has honored notable designers Melitta Baumeister (2023), Christopher John Rogers (2019), and Telfar (2017). The initiative began in 2003 as a post-9/11 effort to support America’s emerging designers. In conjunction with his other accolades from this year, Zane Li’s win at the CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund cements him as one of New York’s most talked-about designers of the moment. a4977d3fa4:3db7c80f30a6ff15.title: YOSHIROTTEN Looks to Outer Space With ‘Transmissions with the Beyond’
a4977d3fa4:3db7c80f30a6ff15.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:3db7c80f30a6ff15.summary: Summary YOSHIROTTEN presents Transmissions with the Beyond at TOKYO NODE, opening October 30, 2026.The show features JAXA-collaborative space art translating astrophysical data into light and sound.Rooftop activations include a Pokémon TCG 30th-anniversary park and cosmic installations. YOSHIROTTEN is extending his long-running investigation into the unseen beyond Earth with Transmissions with the Beyond, his first large-scale solo exhibition in Tokyo in eight years. Running at TOKYO NODE from October 30, 2026 through January 11, 2027, the exhibition fills approximately 1,500 square meters with the artist’s largest presentation to date of his three principal series - RGB, FUTURE NATURE and SUN - alongside an entirely new body of “space art.”Across a career spanning roughly two decades, YOSHIROTTEN has moved fluidly between fine art, graphic design, music, fashion and spatial design, developing a visual language around what he calls the “Visualization of Things Invisible.” Here, that recurring interest in light, color and nature shifts outward, using the vantage point of TOKYO NODE, around 200 meters above the city, as a departure point for thinking about the cosmos.At the center of the exhibition is a collaboration with the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), translating scientific observation into immersive visual experiences. Developed through conversations with Hiroya Yamaguchi of JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science, Puddle Cygnus X-1 transforms observation data from the XRISM mission’s investigation of a black hole into painting and moving image, while "Light Pulse" converts all-sky data captured from the International Space Station into an enveloping installation of light and sound.New works including "Supernova" visualize the explosive life cycle of a star, while Halo renders stellar orbits in sculptural form. The exhibition also brings physical artifacts from Japan’s space program into the gallery, including the solar sail spacecraft…

a4977d3fa4:5562d43e2fb97c29.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:5562d43e2fb97c29.summary: Summary Bose announced its official acquisition of competitor Skullcandy on Wednesday, October 21The strategic purchase aims to capture a younger, action-sports-oriented demographic through the established lifestyle brandSkullcandy will continue to operate as a separate brand within the Bose premium consumer audio business Audio heavyweight Bose has officially announced its official acquisition of competitor Skullcandy. While specific financial details regarding the acquisition were not disclosed, the move signals a strategic shift for the buyer. By absorbing an established lifestyle brand, the historically travel-focused company is actively moving to capture a younger, action-sports-oriented demographic. Rather than dismantling the former rival, Bose confirmed that Skullcandy will continue operating as an entirely separate brand within its premium consumer audio division.Staying true to the lifestyle roots that made it famous, Skullcandy will remain headquartered in Park City, Utah, specifically operating out of the Kimball Junction area. The brand traces its foundation back to a Park City chairlift in 2003, and that mountain-culture DNA is exactly what the new parent company wants to tap into. Moving forward, Bose plans to leverage the distinct product designs of Skullcandy, alongside its deeply rooted relationships with major board sports athletes. Ultimately, the acquisition helps Bose expand its reach to consumers who do not necessarily prioritize active noise cancellation in their daily headphones.Prior to the outright acquisition, the two audio companies engaged in a multiyear partnership that laid the groundwork for this deal. That earlier collaboration integrated the head-tracking spatial audio and active noise cancellation technologies engineered by Bose directly into specific Skullcandy products. Those advanced audio technologies featured in models like the Skullcandy Crusher 1080 ANC headphones and the Method 360 ANC earbuds. According to Bose CEO Lila…

d006da4fe3:7c8255a6f6b6499e.title: The New Energy Stalemate in Ukraine
d006da4fe3:7c8255a6f6b6499e.author: Tatiana Mitrova, Sergey Vakulenko
d006da4fe3:7c8255a6f6b6499e.summary: Tatiana Mitrova, a fellow at Columbia University’s Center on Global Energy Policy and former energy scholar at Moscow’s Russian Academy of Sciences, and Sergey Vakulenko, an oil and gas expert at Carnegie’s Russia Eurasia Center, argue that Russia and Ukraine are locked in an energy war that has become an adaptation spiral, despite growing human and economic costs and despite current US pressure on Ukraine. They observe Ukraine’s remarkable ability to withstand Russian strikes, while questioning claims that long-range Ukrainian strikes will be able to achieve game-changing damage on Russia. Ukraine and Russia have transformed the role of energy warfare in modern conflict, drawing on low costs drones but also new forms of technological resilience that are likely to make wars longer and more dangerous.

d006da4fe3:5ad44315d0de90d6.summary: Monica de Bolle, an expert in Brazilian economic policy, makes an authoritative argument that Brazil’s economic problems will persist no matter the outcome of the country’s presidential election. A Flávio Bolsonaro administration would fare no better than Lula when it comes to reducing debt and delivering growth—and Bolsonaro’s illiberal policies could make the economic picture even worse.

d006da4fe3:d2da9274feed5e6c.title: A Less-Is-More Strategy for America
d006da4fe3:d2da9274feed5e6c.author: Barry R. Posen
d006da4fe3:d2da9274feed5e6c.summary: Barry Posen, a professor at MIT, is one of America's leading experts on international security. He argues that the United States military is breaking down because it has been overused and overextended over the last 30 years, and that the only way to repair it is for Washington to exercise much more restraint.

d006da4fe3:e407454ddc8200e6.title: How Russia Sees the World Now

d006da4fe3:e407454ddc8200e6.summary: Dmitry Adamsky, an expert on Russian security and Russian nuclear deterrence strategy at Harvard and Reichman Universities, examines a large-scale shift in Russia’s strategic thinking over the past year, centered around the view that Europe, rather than the United States, is now Russia’s primary geopolitical rival and adversary, and looking at the consequences of this shift for US efforts to end the war in Ukraine.

d006da4fe3:f2fe497a723c80df.title: AI Is a Choice
d006da4fe3:f2fe497a723c80df.author: Alex Imas, Mohamed A. El-Erian, James Manyika
d006da4fe3:f2fe497a723c80df.summary: Alex Imas, Mohamed El-Erian, and James Manyika, leading voices at the intersection of business and technology, argue that realizing AI’s potential requires giving workers, communities, AI labs, infrastructure developers, and big companies a share of the gains. Using insights from game theory, they argue that increased cooperation can make AI work for all.

d006da4fe3:26bb42beb62831bc.title: The China Price
d006da4fe3:26bb42beb62831bc.author: Zongyuan Zoe Liu
d006da4fe3:26bb42beb62831bc.summary: In 1971, as the international monetary system was on the brink of collapse, U.S. Treasury Secretary John Connally told a group of worried European finance ministers that the dollar was “our currency, but your problem.” The dollar had become that system’s official reserve currency in 1944, under the Bretton Woods agreement, making signatories subject to the whims of U.S. monetary policy. Even after Bretton Woods collapsed and many currencies floated freely, the dollar continued to dominate. In the last half century, U.S. currency power has only expanded, as more countries have integrated into the global economy and therefore grown to depend on the dollar. China, reliant on export-driven growth, is foremost among them.

d006da4fe3:8d3c26580c9ed628.title: Empires of AI
d006da4fe3:8d3c26580c9ed628.author: Niall Ferguson, Lisa Klaassen, Eric Schmidt
d006da4fe3:8d3c26580c9ed628.summary: In this essay, Niall Ferguson, one of the world’s foremost experts on imperial history, teams up the former CEO of Google, Eric Schmidt, and the researcher Lisa Klaasen to make the provocative argument that AI is an inherently “imperial technology”—and to reveal what the fate of past empires might say about the future of U.S.-Chinese competition in a world shaped by AI.

d006da4fe3:33fc15a61a4dba01.title: “Earth Satellites and Foreign Policy”
d006da4fe3:33fc15a61a4dba01.summary: The advent of a new technology invariably comes with strategic implications, raising the question of who will benefit and whether risks can be managed. In 1957, following the Soviet Sputnik launch, U.S. policymakers and analysts recognized that the satellite, as the American physicist and engineer Lloyd Berkner observed in these pages, would bring transformative effects. The United States could not risk losing out, Berkner argued, but nor should governments allow geopolitical tensions to prevent the technology’s broad benefits from emerging.

d006da4fe3:9729d1ab8b25d3aa.title: Europe’s Credibility Gap
d006da4fe3:9729d1ab8b25d3aa.author: Claas Mertens, Ngaire Woods
d006da4fe3:9729d1ab8b25d3aa.summary: Ngaire Woods, Dean of Oxford’s Blavatnik School of Government, Claas Mertens, also at Oxford, have written a piece arguing that Europe, despite its attempts at self-sufficiency, remains dependent on an unpredictable United States. The continent needs to address this vulnerability so that it can convince other countries, many of which find themselves similarly vulnerable to great-power coercion, that it is a worthy partner.

d006da4fe3:09191e7fdf89ba60.title: A Better “America First”
d006da4fe3:09191e7fdf89ba60.author: Charles Kupchan
d006da4fe3:09191e7fdf89ba60.summary: Charles Kupchan, who served in the Clinton and Obama administrations, argues that many aspects of Trump's foreign policy are worth keeping and align with changes in the international system. He explains how the next president can marry the good impulses of "America first" with the best of liberal internationalism.

d006da4fe3:daabdb8037186d1e.title: The Axis of Upheaval Goes to War
d006da4fe3:daabdb8037186d1e.author: Andrea Kendall-Taylor, Richard Fontaine
d006da4fe3:daabdb8037186d1e.summary: Andrea Kendall-Taylor and Richard Fontaine, former members of the National Security Council, argue that the members of what they call the “axis of upheaval”—Russia, China, Iran, and North Korea—are deepening their cooperation. Meanwhile, Washington is creating friction with many of its own partnerships. If these developments continue unabated, the United States will squander the strength of its network just as its adversaries learn to make the most of theirs.

d006da4fe3:960aafc689650ffc.title: The Nuclear Deal That Could Save NATO
d006da4fe3:960aafc689650ffc.author: Ivo H. Daalder
d006da4fe3:960aafc689650ffc.summary: Former U.S. NATO ambassador Ivo Daalder argues that the scramble to shore up Europe's conventional defense risks overlooking the continent's greatest security weakness: nuclear deterrence. Europe knows it can't fully trust Washington's guarantee anymore. But he lays out a middle path between dependence and nuclearization that would extend France's and the United Kingdom's nuclear umbrella—a course, he argues, that could even repair the transatlantic alliance.

d006da4fe3:22627d45ff3f3498.title: The Scramble for the Open Seas
d006da4fe3:22627d45ff3f3498.author: Michael Albertus
d006da4fe3:22627d45ff3f3498.summary: Over the last half millennium, societies around the globe competed to divide up the world’s land. Nearly every square inch of soil outside Antarctica is now owned and tucked within national borders. But the oceans have largely been spared that fate. There were times throughout history when countries tried to gate and regulate the seas, but they were too vast to be controlled for long periods. During the Cold War, as technology made it far easier to imagine partitioning the world’s waterways and seabeds, great powers avoided an unrestrained race to grab the oceans. Most governments agreed to deal with them through a patchwork of treaties and multilateral bodies that sought to guarantee freedom of navigation in international waters and assign coastal seabeds to adjacent littoral states.

d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.title: The Trouble With the Nuclear-AI Analogy
d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.author: Christopher LaRoche, Ankit Panda
d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.summary: In humanity’s quest to constrain the dangers from fast-advancing artificial intelligence, many have looked to the most revolutionary technology that preceded it: nuclear weapons. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has called artificial intelligence “far more dangerous than nukes.” Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who assigns The Making of the Atomic Bomb to employees and has likened himself to the Manhattan Project scientist Leo Szilard, describes the most powerful AI models as “weaponizable nuclear materials.” When asked how a technology such as AI can be regulated, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman often references the world’s nuclear materials watchdog, the International Atomic Energy Agency. Even the director of the CIA, John Ratcliffe, has made the same comparison.These comparisons capture real parallels. Like nuclear weapons, frontier AI is powerful and hard to control. Like nuclear technology, it can be used for good or for ill. And like the Cold War arms race, the race for AI breakthroughs may reorder the global balance of power. The nuclear analogy, then, seems to offer a blueprint for how to effectively govern a promising but potentially dangerous technology such as AI.
